item.title: Lint and Lint Errors
item.description:
What is lint?#

Suppose you write this program:

const total = 10 + 20;
console.log("Done");

Run it. You will see:

Done

The program works. But look at total.

You calculated it and never used it. Perhaps you meant to print it. Perhaps you no longer need that line.

JavaScript does not complain, so how would you notice?

We can use a tool to examine the code we have written.

It does not run the program. Instead, it checks the code against a set of rules to identify potential problems , expected style which we are supposed to write programs in and code-quality issues.

item.title: Style Guide
item.description:
JavaScript Style Guide#

Writing code is not only about making a computer do something. It is also about writing code that another person can read, understand, and change.

This guide describes the conventions we will use when writing JavaScript.

These are not arbitrary rules. Most of them exist because they make code easier to read and reason about.

When you work on an assignment, follow these conventions unless the assignment says otherwise.
